# Measured results

Every number quoted in `papers/` that is not an arithmetic identity or an
explicitly cited literature value is produced by one of these scripts.
Regenerate with `python measure/run_all.py`.

## How big is the space of positions

`measure/counting.py`

Each row adds one constraint to the row above. The `saved` column is the
cost of that constraint in bits, and is the only column worth reading.

```
king pairs (ordered, non-adjacent) = 3612
  by kings on back ranks: {0: 1952, 1: 1448, 2: 212}

bound                                               count     bits   saved
B0  every square holds one of 13 states         1.961e+71   236.83        
B1  + pawns only on ranks 2-7                   1.354e+70   232.97    +3.9
B2  + exactly two kings, non-adjacent           6.000e+66   221.83   +11.1
B3  + <=16 men a side, promotion budget         2.148e+49   163.88   +58.0
B4  x side to move (2)                          4.296e+49   164.88    -1.0
B5  x castling rights (<=16)                    6.873e+50   168.88    -4.0
B6  x en passant file (<=9)                     6.186e+51   172.05    -3.2
```

## What symmetry survives, and what it is worth

`measure/symmetry.py`

`bits saved` is log2 of the mean orbit size: the most a canonical form
could ever save. `ceiling` is log2 of the group order, which it reaches
only when the group acts freely and the family is closed under it.

```
group orders
  no pawns, no castling :  16   (D4 x colour swap)
  pawns on the board    :   4   (file mirror x colour swap)
  castling rights alive :   2   (colour swap only)
  general position      :   1   (nothing survives)

family                                  |X|     orbits  bits saved  ceiling
K vs K            pawnless             7224        462       3.967     4.00
KQ vs K           pawnless           447888      56112       2.997     4.00
KQ vs K / K vs KQ pawnless           895776      56112       3.997     4.00
KP vs K           a pawn             336048     168024       1.000     2.00
KP vs K / K vs KP a pawn             672096     168024       2.000     2.00
KP vs K           castling           336048     336048       0.000     1.00
```

## Bits per ply

`measure/plyrate.py`

Costs that depend only on the number of legal moves, not on which ones.

```
scheme                                bits/ply  bytes/game
SAN text, as in PGN                      40.00       400.0
UCI text, 'e2e4' + separator             40.00       400.0
from|to|promo|flag, 16 bits              16.00       160.0
from|to, 12 bits + escape                12.00       120.0
legal-move index, one byte                8.00        80.0
legal-move index, worst case              7.77        77.7

legal-move index, as a function of the branching factor b
    b  ceil bits  exact bits  bytes/game
    1          0       0.000         0.0
    5          3       2.322        23.2
   10          4       3.322        33.2
   20          5       4.322        43.2
   25          5       4.644        46.4
   30          5       4.907        49.1
   35          6       5.129        51.3
   40          6       5.322        53.2
   60          6       5.907        59.1
  218          8       7.768        77.7

  E[log2 b] over a real corpus is the number that matters and it is
  strictly below log2 E[b] by Jensen. Measuring it is experiment X1.

storing a game as positions instead of moves
  naive 13^64 packing                        236.8 bits x 80 plies =   2.31 KiB/game
  derived bound B6 (counting.py)             172.1 bits x 80 plies =   1.68 KiB/game
  literature estimate of legal positions     148.4 bits x 80 plies =   1.45 KiB/game

pointer into an opening book vs entropy coding the same choice
     256 lines, Zipf s=1 : pointer   8.0 bits, entropy   6.2 bits, waste  1.8
    4096 lines, Zipf s=1 : pointer  12.0 bits, entropy   8.8 bits, waste  3.2
   65536 lines, Zipf s=1 : pointer  16.0 bits, entropy  11.1 bits, waste  4.9
```

## How much of a stored game is chess

`measure/envelope.py`

The move stream compresses; the keys and signatures around it do not.
This is the table that decides how much compression is worth buying.

```
envelope, one attestation per game
  two public keys                     64 bytes
  two signatures                     128 bytes
  result, rules id, clock, date        8 bytes
  total                              200 bytes

move stream                     bytes  +envelope   chess %
PGN text                        400.0      600.0     66.7%
16-bit moves                    160.0      360.0     44.4%
legal index, b = 30              49.1      249.1     19.7%
model-based, 1.7 bits/ply        17.0      217.0      7.8%

envelope per game when games are attested in batches
 batch size  envelope B   chess % at 49 B
          1       200.0             19.7%
         10        26.4             65.0%
        100        17.0             74.2%
       1000        16.1             75.3%
      10000        16.0             75.4%

corpus size at 6e9 games
  PGN text                     per-game attestation     3352.8 GiB
  PGN text                     batched by 1000          2325.2 GiB
  16-bit moves                 per-game attestation     2011.7 GiB
  16-bit moves                 batched by 1000           984.1 GiB
  legal index, b = 30          per-game attestation     1391.8 GiB
  legal index, b = 30          batched by 1000           364.2 GiB
  model-based, 1.7 bits/ply    per-game attestation     1212.6 GiB

```
